chunks: Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

If two witnesses testify before the Imam that they saw the crescent thirty days earlier, the Imam commands the breaking of the fast on that day if they testified before the sun’s zenith. And if they testify after the sun’s zenith, the Imam commands the breaking of the fast on that day and delays the prayer until the next day, then he leads them in prayer.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the prayer, here referring to the ʿĪd prayer
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam, the authority before whom the testimony is presented and who issues the communal ruling
key_terms.الْغَدِ: the next day, to which the prayer is deferred if testimony comes after noon
key_terms.الْهِلَالَ: the crescent moon marking the beginning of the new lunar month
key_terms.بِإِفْطَارِ: breaking the fast, ending the day’s fasting observance
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: the sun’s zenith or noon, the dividing point for the ruling
key_terms.شَاهِدَانِ: two witnesses whose testimony establishes the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if the crescent of ʿĪd al-Fiṭr is confirmed after people have already started fasting that day?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for when the sighting establishing ʿĪd al-Fiṭr is confirmed only after people have already begun the day fasting. If the testimony reaches the Imam before noon, they break the fast that day; if it comes after noon, they still break the fast, but the ʿĪd prayer is postponed until the following day.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2037 - It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (as), who said:

"If two witnesses testify before the Imam that they have seen the crescent moon thirty days ago, the Imam commands the people to break their fast on that day if the testimony is given before noon. However, if they testify after noon, the Imam commands them to break their fast on that day but delays the Eid prayer until the next day, and then he leads them in prayer."
